inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalents, millions. 1 ordinary share = 5 ADSs (Q2-2026 6-K income statement: diluted EPS RMB44.11 per ordinary share vs RMB8.82 per ADS) -- NOT 1:1. Fully diluted ordinary shares at 2026-06-30 = 95.1m outstanding (101.4m issued less 6.3m treasury, 6-K balance-sheet note 4) + 1.378m dilutive securities (Q2-2026 diluted 97,619,760 less basic 96,241,715) = 96.478m, x5 = 482.39m ADS-equivalents. The quarter's weighted-average diluted ADS count was 488.1m; the period-end figure is used because the US$99m of Q2 buybacks has already retired those shares. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so compounding dilution as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (RMB4.9bn FY2025, US$1.0bn programme + new US$1.0bn programme from Aug-2026) fund the flat count and more.
inputs.net_debt_note: At 2026-06-30 (6-K 2026-08-25 balance sheet, RMB m): cash and equivalents 29,246.4 + short-term investments 3,618.5 + held-to-maturity securities 806.4 = 33,671.4 cash-like; less short-term loans 10,968.1 = net cash 22,703.2. Restricted cash (604.9) excluded. Operating lease liabilities (600.7) excluded under lease treatment (B). Short-term loans doubled from 5,844.6 at FY2025 year-end while cash rose 6.3bn: the June-2026 Vipshop Commercial REIT listing brought in ~RMB7.7bn gross proceeds. Interest expense stepped up to RMB243m in Q2-2026 (from 23m), consistent with the larger loan book.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 cash-flow statement add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation = AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, RMB1,731,063k). No PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation concept is tagged in any year and the financing section carries no net-share-settlement line, so the cash-flow add-back is the combined figure. H1-2026 SBC was RMB707m (1.38% of revenue) vs RMB1,048m (2.0%) in H1-2025.
inputs.interest_income_note: InvestmentIncomeInterest FY2025 RMB801.6m (kpis). Stripped because net cash (22.7bn) is ~8x the owner-FCF base; the cash pile is added once, in the bridge. H1-2026 interest income ran RMB360m.
inputs.capital_return_note: FY2025 financing outflows: buybacks RMB4,940.8m + dividends RMB1,795.4m = RMB6.7bn, ~2.3x owner FCF and ~90% of non-GAAP net income, funded from the cash pile. Policy: return no less than 75% of prior-year non-GAAP net income; FY2026 dividend raised to US$0.62/ADS; ~US$400m returned in H1-2026.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY), 20-F filer; ADSs quoted in USD on the NYSE. fx_rate is the engine's reporting->quote multiplier: 1 CNY = US$0.14915, i.e. USDCNY 6.7048 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-10-04T03:30Z), the same rate and date used on TCOM. Company's own convenience-translation rate at 2026-06-30 was RMB6.7851 per US$1 (H.10 noon buying rate), 1.2% weaker RMB -- the rate has moved, not the method. No dual listing exists for a parity check, so the check is internal: FY2025 diluted EPS RMB72.37 per ordinary share / 5 = RMB14.47 per ADS = US$2.16 per ADS at 6.7048, giving a trailing P/E of 5.7x at the current price, consistent with the 4-6x range third-party screens report (info.json: P/E 4.1 on a different earnings basis). A 1:1 ADS assumption would give a P/E of 1.1x, which is the error this check exists to catch. Per-ADS values in CNY are emitted as *_cny twins; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are USD per ADS, comparable to current_price. scripts/sanity_check.py uses the reciprocal convention (quote->reporting, 6.7048) for its historical table -- see memory note sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-conflict.
inputs.ads_ratio_note: sanity_check.py's multiples() defines ads_ratio as ordinary shares PER ADS (its docstring example: NTES 1 ADS = 5 ordinary -> ads_ratio=5) and divides shares_outstanding by it. VIPS is the inverse ratio -- 1 ordinary share = 5 ADSs, i.e. 0.2 ordinary shares per ADS (see fx_note) -- so ads_ratio=0.2 here, not 5. core_metrics.shares_outstanding is always the company's own ordinary-share count (e.g. FY2025 102.38m); dividing by 0.2 gives 511.9m ADS-equivalents, consistent with the dcf-analyst's independently-derived 482.39m period-end figure (small difference is diluted securities/buyback timing, not a basis error), so the historical P/B and P/E are not inflated 5x against the per-ADS price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation date falls on the weekend, no after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency, on the same basis as the TCOM build: 10y China government bond ~1.8% risk-free + beta 1.2 x (mature-market ERP 5.0% + China country risk premium ~1.8%) = ~10.0% cost of equity; ~95% equity weight at market, ~2% after-tax cost of RMB bank debt -> WACC ~9.6%, rounded up to 10.0%. The country premium is the only China charge in the rate. Share loss, apparel-category cyclicality, VIE/HFCAA/ADR risk are charged ONCE, in the flows, via the 30% bear weight and the bear driver path -- the same 10.0% WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost (RMB90.7m FY2025, total lease cost RMB225.0m incl. short-term and variable) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; operating lease liabilities (RMB600.7m at 2026-06-30) are excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is PP&E depreciation + intangible + land-use-right amortisation, ex right-of-use. Charged exactly once. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed because the cost is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows. NCI share of profit was RMB167m in FY2025 (2.3% of net income) and RMB91m in H1-2026, mostly the minority in Shan Shan Outlets; the NCI stock of RMB3,344.8m at 2026-06-30 is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge. Not folded into the tax path.
inputs.da_note: FY2025 D&A used for the 1.7% anchor: PP&E depreciation RMB1,526.5m + intangible amortisation 3.8m (XBRL) + land-use-right amortisation estimated ~250m (land use rights RMB10.4bn net at FY2025, 40-50 year terms; no separate XBRL concept) = ~1,780m = 1.68% of revenue. EBIT check: EBITDA 11,647 - SBC 1,731 - D&A 1,780 = 8,136 ties to GAAP income from operations RMB8,135.9m.
inputs.tax_note: Cash taxes paid FY2025 RMB2,443.1m (IncomeTaxesPaidNet) against EBIT of 8,136 = 30%; FY2024 2,169 on 9,173 = 24%; GAAP effective rate 20.2% FY2025 (on a pre-tax base that includes RMB802m of interest income and RMB294m of equity-method income, both outside the flows). Statutory 25% PRC EIT with 15% HNTE rates for some subsidiaries, PLUS withholding tax on dividends upstreamed from PRC subsidiaries to fund the US$1bn+/yr shareholder return -- the RMB1.56bn Q2-2026 accrual reflects a 10% rather than 5% treaty rate on historical distributions and signals that rate going forward. Base cash tax 28% on EBIT; bear 30%; bull 27%.
inputs.working_capital_note: Payables-funded retailer: accounts payable 10.4bn + accrued 10.8bn + advances 1.4bn against inventory 4.3bn + receivables ~3.0bn at 2026-06-30. Revenue growth releases cash and revenue decline consumes it (FY2023 +9.7bn revenue, ~+2.7bn WC inflow; FY2024/25 declines, ~-3bn/yr outflows, partly internet-financing receivables the company's own FCF definition adds back). wc_capture_pct is POSITIVE 20% of the revenue change, so the bear path's shrinking top line is charged an annual WC outflow and the bull path's growth is credited a smaller inflow.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1-2: operating company, consumer internet, non-US filer, adaptations (a) currency, (b) leases, (c) NCI, (d) matching asset applied). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Vipshop is an off-price branded-apparel flash-sales retailer in China (Vip.com ~90% of revenue) plus Shan Shan Outlets (22 physical outlet malls, 20%+ GMV growth). FY2025 anchors: revenue 105,920 (-2.3%), GAAP income from operations 8,136 (7.7%), pre-SBC EBITDA ~11,647 (11.0%), SBC 1,731 (1.6%), capex 1,986 (1.9%), OCF 7,454, reported FCF 5,468 and owner FCF 2,936 after SBC and interest income -- the FY2025 owner FCF is depressed by a ~3.5bn working-capital outflow (payables unwinding on falling sales); TTM-to-June-2026 company-defined FCF was 7,202 (OCF 8,766 - capex 1,513 + 52 internet-financing add-back), i.e. ~5.1bn on an owner basis, which is why the projection is built from components rather than from last_fcf. Buybacks fund the flat count (RMB4.9bn FY2025, > SBC 1.7bn). Q2-2026 one-offs excluded from the flows: RMB5.79bn investment gain on the Vipshop Commercial REIT listing (and its RMB1.63bn tax), the RMB1.56bn withholding-tax catch-up (its run-rate effect is in the 28% cash tax rate), and the deconsolidation of two Shan Shan outlets into the REIT (small revenue/EBITDA loss from June 2026, absorbed in the FY2026 growth and margin path). Street basis differs from house by the SBC charge only. Valuation runs in CNY per ADS then converts at fx_rate; see fx_note. The 2026-10-02 close is a regular Friday close, not volatile.

equity_bridge.item: Investment in equity-method investees at book (includes the 49% stake in the SSE-listed Vipshop Commercial REIT, fund 508603.SH, subscribed June 2026)
equity_bridge.note: 6-K 2026-08-25 balance sheet at 2026-06-30, RMB7,616.2m (up from 3,136.8m at FY2025 on the REIT subscription). Equity-method income (RMB294m FY2025, RMB558m H1-2026 incl. REIT) and the outlets' rent now sit outside EBITDA, so the matching-asset rule puts the asset in the bridge at book. The REIT units are listed at the subscription price; the remainder is unlisted JV stakes at book.
RMB3,344.8m at 2026-06-30 (6-K balance sheet), mostly the Shan Shan Outlets minority. Flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here.

equity_bridge.item: Other investments (fair-value and cost-method stakes) -- EXCLUDED, carried at zero
equity_bridge.note: RMB4,980.9m at 2026-06-30. Unlisted, illiquid, investment gains/losses and impairments are outside the flows; held at zero as a deliberate conservatism rather than a haircut. Worth ~US$1.5/ADS at book if a reader wants to add it back.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year average of the growth path (-2% FY2026 guided slightly negative, flat by FY2028, 2% from FY2031); NOT the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (8.6% 5yr) diverges by >30% from revenue CAGR (0.8%) and the owner-FCF CAGR (-18.5%). Equity compounds because the company retains ~10% of earnings after a ~90% payout and because NCI jumped RMB1.9bn in FY2025 (Shan Shan minorities); it says nothing about the top line, which has been flat for five years and is now guided down. EPS CAGR (10.6%) is almost entirely buyback-driven: net income grew 4.6%/yr while the diluted count fell 5.8%/yr. The equity CAGR is therefore rejected as the forward growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income, RMB m): FY2020 8,183; FY2021 2,331; FY2022 6,117; FY2023 9,957; FY2024 4,058; FY2025 2,936. The owner-FCF CAGR (-18.5% 5yr) is well below the reported-FCF CAGR (-10.6%): SBC rose from 951 to 1,731 (0.9% to 1.6% of revenue) while interest income nearly doubled, so a growing share of reported FCF is comp paid in stock and income on the cash pile. The series is also dominated by working-capital swings (+2.7bn FY2023, ~-3bn FY2024 and FY2025) that track the direction of revenue; the component build normalises these.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -2.0%: H1-2026 revenue -1.5% (51,282 vs 52,075), Q3 guided RMB20.3-21.4bn (-5% to 0%), management says full year 'slightly negative', and two outlets left the consolidation in June. FY2027 -1% as active-customer attrition (-2.9% YoY, orders -5.5%) is only partly offset by SVIP spend and Shan Shan; flat by FY2028; 1-2% from FY2029 as the business tracks a slow-growing Chinese apparel market with the outlet chain adding ~1pt. Terminal 2% in CNY.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 11.4% FY2024, 11.0% FY2025, ~11.0% H1-2026 (non-GAAP operating margin 9.2% vs 9.6%). FY2026 10.6% for the Q2 step-down (8.1% vs 9.3% non-GAAP operating margin: return rates, fulfilment cost, lost leverage) and the outlet deconsolidation; 10.5% held flat thereafter -- cost discipline and SVIP mix offset deleverage but do not restore the FY2024 peak. SBC 1.45% (H1-2026 run-rate 1.38%, FY2025 1.63%) gliding to 1.3%. Capex 1.8-1.9% (FY2023-25 1.9/2.5/1.9%, TTM 1.4%) roughly matching D&A 1.7%.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at the top of guidance (-1%), Chinese discretionary spending stabilises in 2027, SVIP (10m members, +8%, 54% of online spend) keeps growing spend per member, Shan Shan Outlets compounds at 20%+ GMV and reaches ~10% of revenue, and the Tencent/JD channels hold online share. 3-3.5% growth FY2028-30, 2.5% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Mix shift to SVIP and outlets plus AI-driven merchandising lifts the pre-SBC EBITDA margin back to and slightly above the FY2024 11.4% peak; returns normalise. Capex 2% for outlet expansion; cash tax 27% with more HNTE-rated profit.

bear.growth_rationale: Q3 comes in at the bottom of guidance (-5%) and the decline accelerates: Douyin livestream commerce, PDD subsidies and JD/Taotian discount apparel keep taking the mass-market customer (active customers fall ~3-5%/yr), SVIP growth stalls, Chinese apparel spending stays deflationary. Revenue falls ~17% cumulatively to ~RMB88bn by FY2031 before flattening; terminal 1%.
bear.margin_rationale: Operating deleverage on a fixed fulfilment and outlet cost base, rising return rates and marketing spend to defend traffic compress the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 11% to 9%; SBC held at 1.5% as the share price falls (more units per RMB); cash tax 30% as dividend withholding runs at the 10% rate on a larger repatriated share. Terminal cap 10x for a shrinking business.

scenario_narratives.base: Vipshop stays a niche off-price apparel platform in slow structural decline: revenue drifts down ~3% over two years as active customers shrink, then stabilises around RMB104-108bn from FY2028 as the 10m-member SVIP cohort and the Shan Shan outlet chain (22 malls, 20%+ GMV growth) offset mass-market attrition to Douyin, PDD and JD. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin settles at 10.5%, just under the FY2024-25 11-11.4% range, SBC glides from 1.5% to 1.3% of revenue, capex and D&A run near parity at ~1.8%, and cash tax runs at 28% once the 10% dividend withholding rate is applied to the profits upstreamed each year to fund the ~US$1bn capital return. Owner FCF of ~RMB5-6bn a year is capitalised at 12x (the cap binds, below the 12.75x Gordon value at 10%/2%). Axes: active-customer attrition vs SVIP spend; apparel-category cyclicality; whether margins can be defended as revenue falls.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chinese discretionary consumption stabilises in 2027 and Vipshop's deep brand-supply relationships make it the natural clearance channel as brands carry excess inventory; SVIP spend per member keeps compounding, Shan Shan Outlets scales toward ~10% of revenue with real-estate-like economics (and the REIT provides recycled capital for more outlets), and the Tencent/JD traffic channels hold online share. Growth returns to 3-3.5% in FY2028-30, the margin recovers above the FY2024 peak to 11.5%, and the terminal value is Gordon at 10%/2.5% (13.7x, under the 14x cap). Needs three things to go right at once -- macro, share stabilisation, and the outlet build-out -- hence 20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The core flash-sale niche is absorbed by larger platforms: Douyin's livestream apparel, PDD's subsidies and JD/Taotian's discount pushes keep pulling the value-seeking customer, active users fall 3-5% a year, orders decline faster than GMV, and apparel (75% of GMV) stays deflationary. Revenue shrinks ~17% to ~RMB88bn by FY2031 and flattens; the fixed fulfilment and outlet cost base pushes the EBITDA margin to 9%, return rates and defensive marketing rise, and the working-capital unwind on falling sales is charged every year. Capitalised at 10x with 1% terminal growth. The China ADR structural tail (HFCAA, VIE, geopolitics) is why this path carries 30% rather than the house 15%; even here the net cash and investments (~RMB27bn, ~US$8/ADS) are a floor the price already sits near.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the top line is in a management-guided decline with active customers and orders falling, the competitive threat (Douyin, PDD, JD, Taotian) is structural rather than cyclical, apparel is 75% of GMV, and the ticker carries the China ADR tail (HFCAA audit access, VIE enforceability, geopolitics) on top -- the same tail that puts TCOM at 30%. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs an independent macro recovery, share stabilisation against better-capitalised rivals, and the outlet build-out all to land. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A shrinking but highly cash-generative off-price retailer trading as if the equity were worth little more than its cash. At the 2026-10-02 close the market capitalisation is ~US$5.9bn (RMB39.9bn), against net cash of RMB22.7bn plus RMB7.6bn of equity-method investments (net of RMB3.3bn NCI, ~RMB27bn or ~US$8/ADS of balance-sheet value), so the operating business -- RMB8bn of GAAP operating profit, ~RMB5bn of normalised owner FCF -- is priced at roughly 2-3x. The house DCF values the flows in CNY at a 10% WACC with the China/ADR risk charged once through a 30% bear weight, capitalises the terminal year at a deliberately low 10-14x cap, excludes RMB5bn of other investments at zero, and still arrives well above the price in every scenario, including the bear. That gap is the price of the China-ADR discount and of the structural-decline narrative, not of any aggressive assumption: SBC is fully expensed, the share count is held flat despite RMB4.9bn/yr of buybacks, and interest income is stripped. The required-return table shows what discount rate the current price implies; a reader who believes the cash will never reach ADS holders should read the bear entry price, not the weighted IV. A no-re-rate memo: capitalising the terminal year at the stock's own recent ~3x EV/EBITDA instead of 12x would still leave the base value above the price, because two-thirds of the market cap is balance-sheet cash and investments.
key_risks_to_valuation: Structural share loss to Douyin, Pinduoduo, JD and Taotian in discount apparel; active customers -2.9% and orders -5.5% YoY in Q2-2026, with management guiding FY2026 revenue slightly negative
Apparel is ~75% of GMV: a prolonged Chinese discretionary-spending slump or apparel deflation hits both volume and margin
Operating deleverage: Q2-2026 non-GAAP operating margin fell to 8.1% from 9.3% on rising return rates and fulfilment cost; a 1pt margin miss is ~RMB1bn of EBITDA

Cash-trapping and tax leakage: profits sit in PRC subsidiaries; dividend withholding tax (RMB1.56bn catch-up accrued Q2-2026 at the 10% rate) raises the cash cost of the US$1bn+/yr return programme, modelled as a 28-30% cash tax rate
China ADR structural tail: HFCAA audit-inspection contingency, VIE enforceability, US-China geopolitics; priced via the 30% bear weight, not the WACC
RMB/USD: flows are CNY, the quote is USD; a 10% RMB depreciation cuts every USD figure here by 10% with no offset

Balance-sheet value assumptions: RMB7.6bn equity-method investees (incl. the 49% REIT stake) taken at book, RMB5.0bn other investments at zero; short-term loans doubled to RMB11bn in H1-2026 and must stay matched by cash
Working-capital unwind: a payables-funded model consumes cash as revenue falls (FY2024-25 ~RMB3bn/yr); the 20% capture rate may understate the outflow if the decline accelerates
